mia: Quick run summary for llama-2-13b quant onboarding (INT8) across US-EAST / US-WEST / EU-WEST on H100 / A100. Posting p50/p95 + short notes.

mia: TL;DR: p50s are fine everywhere (~30-45ms batch=1); p95 in EU-W has a 60-90ms tail increase vs US that looks correlated with proxy hop + kernel fallback on A100. H100 int8 path much smoother.

mia: Raw snapshot (batch=1, seq=512, kv-cache cold start averaged into numbers):
```
Region  GPU   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  QPS(single GPU)
USEAST  H100  32       48       180
USEAST  A100  38       67       140
USWEST  H100  34       50       175
USWEST  A100  40       72       135
EUWEST  H100  36       60       165
EUWEST  A100  45       130      110  <-- noticeable p95 jump
```

mia: Observations: EUWEST/A100 p95 spike correlates with edge-proxy egress via secondary pop (extra hop, ~12ms) + kernel fallback to slower GEMM path intermittently under warmup. H100 int8 kernel stays on optimized path.

aj: Do you have the exact curl/bench command and flag set? Was auto-routing enabled or pinned?

mia: bench command: `./bench --model llama-2-13b-int8 --seq 512 --batch 1 --iters 500 --warmup 100 --gpu H100/A100 --region <pop>`
Routing flags: most runs use `--edge-routing auto` (so requests may go via nearest proxy). I also ran pinned runs (`--edge-routing direct`) that removed the EU p95 spike almost entirely on A100.

ralph: Could be kernel selection noise + kernel cache churn on A100. Do we see any logs showing fallback messages?

mia: yes, grep from runtime logs: `kernel_select: fallback_to_gemm=true` shows intermittency in EUWEST A100 runs, coincident with higher p95. timestamps align with canary proxy failover logs.

sophia: Any eval delta after quant? We need to know if quality hit is in-bounds before promoting.

mia: ran a quick eval on our canonical prompt-set (500 examples) — int8 had mean score drop ~0.4% (within guardrail of 1.0%) but some prompts showed regression >2% (edge cases). Logging examples to S3: s3://redwood-evals/llama2-13b/int8/warmup-2026-03-17.log

luis: For capacity planning: what does this mean for Dedicated sizing if a customer in EU wants 99th pct latency SLA?

mia: For EU with strict p95 SLA, prefer pinning to direct POPs + H100. If locked to A100 we estimate ~1.6x GPU count due to tail amplification (based on effective QPS drop from 140->110). So recommend reserve 60-70% additional capacity if using A100 without routing pin.

aj: Can you attach the raw CSV of per-request latencies? I'll run our tail decomposition script.

mia: Uploaded CSVs to: https://internal.redwood/benchmarks/1735550999/ (csvs: useast_h100.csv, useast_a100.csv, usw_h100.csv, usw_a100.csv, euw_h100.csv, euw_a100.csv)

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: quant-llama2-13b-int8 -> dedicated/qa-pool (3 GPUs) started by mia at 2026-03-17T14:22Z

ralph: Also worth checking kernel build flags for A100 nightly; there was a change two weeks ago that may cause less stable kernel selection under certain sequence-length distributions.

mia: Agreed. Next steps I propose: 1) re-run EUWEST A100 with `--edge-routing direct` + `--kernel-debug=select-trace` to capture selection traces 2) run LRU cache warmup pass (1000 synthetic prompts) then remeasure 3) triage top 20 regressed prompts from eval against float baseline.

sophia: I'll take the eval triage (examples + diff outputs). Assigning to `@sophia` in tracker.

aj: I'll run tail-decomp on the CSVs and post flamegraph. If the extra hop is the main cause we should see a ~10-15ms constant shift for affected requests.

mia: sounds good. I'll schedule the reruns and post updated numbers by EOD. Thanks all :thumbsup:
